what: Scope §2 of Issue #361 and criterion 4: the full list of places checked for the defect class «a readonly field whose type is a mutable struct», recorded before the fix so that the list stands independently of what turned out to be broken.

base.howObtained: git -C C:/gamedev/_wt-361-combat-random rev-parse --short HEAD, taken on the worktree created from origin/main before any edit

whyThisIsTheWholeSearchSpace: A readonly field only suffers the defensive-copy defect when its declared type is a value type that has mutable state. A readonly field of a reference type (class, interface, array, delegate, string) is never copied on member access, and a readonly field of an immutable value type has no state to lose.

So the search is closed by two enumerations: (a) every struct type the repository declares, split into mutable and immutable; (b) every readonly field declaration in src/**, split by whether its declared type is a value type.
External value types (BCL, Godot) are covered by (b): the enumeration is over field declarations, not over our own types, so a readonly field of e.g. Godot.Vector2 would appear in it. None does.

enumerationA.question: which struct types does src/** declare, and which of them are mutable?

immutable.why: All 21 are declared `readonly record struct`. The compiler rejects any mutating instance member on a readonly struct, so a readonly field of one cannot lose a write — there is no write to lose.

types.mutableStateWhy: five public instance fields, all written in SimulationWorld.Step

enumerationB.note: 23 of the 114 hits are the struct type declarations of enumeration A (they contain the word `readonly` in `readonly record struct`), not fields. The remaining 91 are field declarations.

DeterministicRandom is mutable (enumeration A). Every call of _combatRandom.NextInt32 through this field is made on a defensive copy, so _state never moves and CombatJitter returns the same number for the whole party.

referenceTypedReadonlyFields.why: Arrays (including AgentState[] and Side[]), List, Dictionary, SortedDictionary, HashSet, SortedSet, StringBuilder, string[], double[], sealed records and classes. A readonly field of a reference type is never defensively copied: readonly freezes the reference, not the object, and array elements are reached through the reference, not through a copy of it.

the field type is an array, a reference type. The elements are mutated through `ref var agent = ref _agents[index]` (SimulationWorld.cs:76, :206), which reaches the element in place. The two `ref readonly` uses at :119 and :133 only read.

notSearched.why: Issue #361 scope §2 names src/** . For completeness, searching the word `struct` over tests, tools and spikes returns exactly one hit and it is a comment (tests/DungeonFortress.Simulation.Tests/PrototypePostCombatDispersalTests.cs:739). No struct is declared outside src/**, so no mutable struct exists there to be held in a readonly field.

conclusion: One defect in src/**: src/DungeonFortress.Simulation/PrototypeWorld.cs:43. Four other value-typed readonly fields and four other holders of a mutable struct were checked and are clean.
